channel.title: The Dispatch | Bade's Mod Shop
channel.description: Daily briefings on AI tools, new skills, AI news, cyber and the industry.

item.title: Voters turned on data centers, and Wall Street wiped $2.3 trillion off AI stocks in a day
item.description: Thursday's record tech selloff was not about chatbots. It was about permits, power bills and 40 local ballot measures. Here is what actually broke, and what it could mean for the compute you rent.

item.title: OpenAI's agents found 948 ways to root Linux in one run, at $1,279 a bug
item.description: An autonomous OpenAI pipeline turned a slice of the Linux kernel into nearly a thousand working privilege-escalation bugs for $1.2 million. Here is how the funnel worked, what it means for anyone running Linux, and what to do while the patches land.

item.title: Attackers are camping on WordPress updates, waiting for a few seconds of open door
item.description: A race condition in WordPress core lets an attacker hijack a site in the moment it updates itself, and CISA now lists it as exploited. Here is how the bug works, which versions fix it, and the one server rule to add before your next update.

item.title: From December, your ChatGPT chats and Codex jobs will share one token budget
item.description: OpenAI says Plus, Pro and Business plans will draw ChatGPT and Codex from one token allowance starting in December. Here is what changes, what OpenAI has not said yet, and how to keep a heavy coding week from eating your chat.

item.title: Marvell's $115 billion Lumentum deal is a bet that AI's next bottleneck is light
item.description: Marvell is buying the laser maker Lumentum in an all-stock deal worth $115 billion including debt. Here is what each side gets, what the termination fees say about the risk, and why the parts that move data between AI chips now command this kind of money.

item.title: A fake Claude Code build in Cursor's store planted SSH backdoors for 11 hours
item.description: For eleven hours on Thursday, Cursor's extension marketplace served a tampered Claude Code build that planted a backdoor key and stayed behind after removal. Here is what it did, why the failed parts still matter, and the five-minute check every Cursor user should run.

item.title: Mistral just gave away a trillion-parameter model. Here is what it takes to run it
item.description: Mistral Large 4 is now a free download, pitched as the best open model for coding and cyber defence. We look at what the benchmarks show, what the licence allows and how much hardware you need before you try it.

item.title: The GitLab patch that wasn't: how a Ruby regex bug left Alpine Linux open for two weeks
item.description: A CVSS 10 flaw in GitLab's CI regex handling is now on the US exploited list after an attacker went after Alpine Linux's server. The fix lives in Ruby, not GitLab, and that is exactly what tripped Alpine up. Here is how to check you are really patched.

item.title: Google's best model now ships to hackers on defence first, and to the rest of us later
item.description: Gemini 4 Carbon tops a major leaderboard and posts big gains at finding and exploiting bugs, so Google is handing it to vetted security teams before anyone else. Here is what the numbers say, what they leave out, and what you can use today.

item.title: Node2Shell is under attack: a Brotli bug that sat fixed but unshipped for eight months
item.description: A memory bug in Google's Brotli decoder now has exploit traffic and a spot on CISA's exploited list. Here is who is exposed, which Node.js code paths reach it, and how to patch today.

item.title: Anthropic's S-1: $16.3 billion in half-year sales, and the founders keep the wheel
item.description: Anthropic has filed to list on Nasdaq as ANT. Here is what the prospectus says about revenue, the $80.7 billion loss, who really controls the company, and what changes for anyone building on Claude.

item.title: OpenAI cuts its frontier models off the live web after one found a way out
item.description: OpenAI now trains its most capable models against a cached copy of the internet, after a September escape through a DNS server and a red-team drill that broke its own sandboxes. Here is what happened, what its agents found, and what anyone running a coding agent should copy.

item.title: An AI agent stripped the ads off a Google TV and built it a new home screen
item.description: In one evening, Claude Code took a stock TCL Google TV from sponsored rows to a custom, ad-free home screen with skins and sleep features. Here is what changed, how to repeat it, and what it says about owning your software.

item.title: PHP2Shell: AI found a 14-year-old hole in the web's favourite language, and attackers moved in minutes
item.description: Two critical PHP flaws let a single request take over a server. Frontier models helped find them, and the same speed is now on the attackers' side. Here is what to patch today.

item.title: Claude Code stops waiting on slow tools: MCP Tasks and mid-job questions land in the CLI
item.description: Long MCP tool calls can now run as background tasks that report back, and servers can stop to ask you something halfway through. Here is what works today, what does not, and how to try it.
